newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: SOUTHERN AFRICA TO SELL ITSELF AT INVESTMENT MEET.
newsitem.headline: SOUTHERN AFRICA TO SELL ITSELF AT INVESTMENT MEET.

text.p: Southern Africa hosts over 200 leading world business executives in Zimbabwe next week at a conference called to market the region as a viable foreign investment destination.

Some 500 delegates are expected at the three-day Southern African Economic Summit starting next Tuesday, where organisers say discussions will focus on investment opportunities, regional economic potential, infrastructure development and privatisation programmes.

The meeting will also dwell on efforts to integrate the economies of the 12-nation Southern African Development Community (SADC), says Isaac Takawira, the Zimbabwean chairman of the conference organising committee.
"We are looking at this conference as a big opportunity to market our region as the ideal place for investment. That will be the main focus of our presentations and discussions," he told Reuters.
"I have no doubt we will be able to do this. We are assembling our top personalities, both in business and in politics, for this," he added.
The world business community, he said, should also see SADC, with a combined population of over 130 million, as a viable trading partner.

Takawira said the Southern African Economic Summit -- organised by the Geneva-based World Economic Forum -- would be officially opened by South African President Nelson Mandela, the current chairman of SADC.
SADC consists of Angola, Botswana, Malawi, Mozambique, Mauritius, Lesotho, Namibia, Tanzania, South Africa, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

Mandela will be joined by Zimbabwe President Robert in leading a discussion on their political vision of southern Africa, which many regional economic analysts say has the potential to become one of the world's preferred investment sites over the next 10 years.
The conference will also be attended by top officials from the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
